raw_response:
I’m 62 this year, and I’ve farmed this land a long time. I don’t read many fancy recommendations. I mostly do what has worked on my own fields, and I watch what the better farmers nearby are doing. This year I’ll still keep the wheat-maize rotation on the main piece, because that is the steady way to keep grain coming in. Cotton I will keep on part of the land for cash, and mungbean on a small piece because it doesn’t cost much and it helps spread risk. Money is not unlimited, and some people in my family work outside, so I can’t make the plan too heavy on cash or labor. I have a well, so if the weather turns dry, I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I won’t water more than needed.

For wheat, I’ll do close to what I did last year: sow in early October, use a local good seed, put most fertilizer at the start, then give one more topdressing if the stand looks a little weak after winter. Wheat is still the base crop for the family, so I won’t cut inputs too much. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll plant summer maize right away on the same 6 mu. The turnaround is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and fast. For cotton, I’ll stay a bit cautious. Cotton can make money, but it needs more watching and more sprays if insects come. I won’t expand it. Mungbean I’ll keep on a small area because the cost is light, it doesn’t need much fertilizer, and if one crop price is bad, at least I have something else.
